North American Q3 robot orders rise 24.8%, A3 reports

Orders reached 10,989 units worth $723.5 million, led by strong automotive-component and electronics demand.

RoboticsTomorrow ↗28 October 2026English editorial summary
Story

Orders strengthen

A3 reported 10,989 North American robot orders worth $723.5 million in Q3, up 24.8% in units and 26.1% in value year over year. Nine-month orders reached 28,984 units and about $1.89 billion. These are orders, not completed installations.

Industries diverge

Automotive-component orders rose 90.4%, and semiconductors, electronics and photonics rose 97.6%. Automotive OEM orders grew 7.5% in the quarter but remained 17% lower over nine months. Food and consumer goods declined 23.7%, illustrating uneven demand.

Collaborative robots expand

Cobots accounted for 1,831 units worth $63.8 million, approximately 56% unit growth and 16.7% of quarterly robot orders. The figures indicate automation demand rather than guaranteed project returns or a direct measure of Thailand’s market.
